Order 
This Criminal Miscellaneous Case has been filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (`BNSS' for short) by the accused in Crime No.242/2020 of Kilikollur Police Station, Kollam District, seeking quashment of Annexure-A1 FIR and Annexure-A2 final report in the above crime pending as S.C.No.942/2021 on the files of Fast Track Special Court,
Kollam.

2. In this matter, the petitioners, who are arrayed as accused 1 and 2 in the above crime, alleged to have committed offences punishable under Sections 376 r/w 109 and 417 of the Indian Penal Code (`IPC' for short).
The specific case of the prosecution is that the 1 st accused made acquaintance with the defacto complainant and continued the relationship through phone.

Thereafter, with intention to subject her to sexual intercourse so as to satisfy his lust, the 1st accused promised to marry the defacto complainant and also offered to give financial aid for the marriage 2024:KER:83533 of the defacto complainant's daughter.
When the defacto complainant was intimated through telephone to reach the house of the 2 nd accused to receive financial aid, on 27.06.2019.
When the defacto complainant reached the house of the 2nd accused, as informed, the 1st accused subjected her to penetrative sexual assault and thereafter retracted from the marriage.
The specific allegation against the 2nd accused is that the 2nd accused facilitated sexual assault at the instance of the 1 st accused and thereby abetted the crime.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the defacto complainant and the 1st petitioner are adult persons knowing the consequence of the relationship.

According to the learned counsel,
the defacto complainant, who is capable of understanding the nature of the relationship, consented for sexual intercourse and after elapse of 9 months, she filed this complaint which led to registration of Annexure A1 FIR on 10.03.2020, raising false allegations.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the relationship, if any, is purely consensual and therefore the offences alleged would not attract.
He has pointed out the decisions of the Apex Court in [2019(1) KHC 403 in Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar 2024:KER:83533 (Dr.) v. State of Maharashtra and Ors.

sentences.text: And Mandar Deepak Pawar v. The State of Maharashtra and another and the decision of this Hon'ble Court in [2021(1) KHC 195], Ranjith v. State of Kerala, to contend that if the accused has not made the promise with sole intention to seduce the prosecutrix to indulge in sexual acts, such an act would not amount to rape, acknowledged consensual physical relationship between the parties would not constitute an offence under Section 376 of IPC.

sentences.text:
The facts and circumstances of the case categorically show that there was free will and the consent was voluntary,
the offence of rape is not attracted.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, in a catena of decisions, the Apex Court authoritatively pronounced the law that failure to fulfill the marriage and by consensus sex doesn't amount to offence under Section 376 of IPC.

In the absence of any allegations or evidence to show that the 2024:KER:83533 representation was deliberately made by the accused with a view to elicit the assent of the victim without having the intention or inclination to marry her, the offence of rape cannot be attracted.

4. It is submitted further that the decision reported in [AIR 1994 (SC) 604, State of Haryana v.
Bhajanlal, the Apex Court held that when the allegations on the face of it do not made out any offence against an accused or when the proceedings are actuated by manifest malafides, the same can be quashed by a court as abuse of process of the court in the interest of justice.

entities.text:
AIR 1994 (SC) 604, State of Haryana v.
Bhajanlal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case at hand squarely would come into the said category, warranting interference at the hands of this Court.

5. Opposing quashment of the proceedings on finding same as a relationship arose out of consent,
the learned Public Prosecutor would submit that the defacto complainant is a lady, who married earlier, and she was divorced by her earlier husband.
Therefore, she was forced to get money from various persons by using the letter given by South Aryad Mahal Muslim Jama-ath to maintain her children.
During this period the 1st accused made acquaintanance with the defacto complainant and promised to marry her.
On this promise she was subjecteed to rape on 2024:KER:83533 27.06.2019 and the same was abetted by the 2 nd accused.
Thereafter the 1st accused deviated from the marriage and thereby committed the offence alleged.

As per the statement given by the defacto complainant, the prosecution case is specifically made out and in such a case quashment of the proceedings could not be allowed as prosecution has the right to adduce evidence to prove the allegations.
6. On perusal of the case diary, the submission made by the learned Public Prosecutor appears to be convincing.
It is true that going through the prosecution allegation it is specifically clear that the 1 st accused promised to marry the defacto complainant, who is in penury.
Further the accused offered financial aid for the marriage of the daughter of the defacto complainant and later she was subjected to sexual intercourse on the promise of marriage.
But he deviated thereafter from the marriage.
Thus, prima facie, the offences are made out.
In such a case, quashment of the proceedings could not be opted and the matter would require trial.
7. In view of the aforesaid reasons, this Crl.M.C stands dismissed.
Registry shall forward a copy of this order to the jurisdictional court for information and further steps.
